text_blocks.snippet: Type 2 diabetes is treated through lifestyle changes, blood sugar monitoring, medications, and sometimes surgery.
snippet_highlighted_words: lifestyle changes, blood sugar monitoring, medications, and sometimes surgery

list.snippet: Healthy diet: Eat a balanced diet rich in lean proteins, non-starchy vegetables, and complex carbohydrates.
Regular exercise: Get at least 150 minutes of aerobic and strength physical activity each week.
Weight loss: Aim to lose 5% or more of your body weight to improve blood sugar control.
Blood sugar tracking: Monitor your glucose levels regularly using a home meter or a continuous glucose monitor.
Metformin: This is the most common first-line oral medication. It lowers glucose production in the liver and improves insulin sensitivity.
GLP-1 receptor agonists: These injectable or oral drugs help lower blood sugar and support weight loss.
SGLT2 inhibitors: These pills help your kidneys remove excess sugar through urine while protecting heart and kidney health.
Other oral options: Sulfonylureas, DPP-4 inhibitors, and thiazolidinediones stimulate insulin release or boost insulin sensitivity.
Insulin therapy: Synthetic insulin injections or pumps are used if other medications do not control blood sugar effectively.
Weight-loss (bariatric) surgery: This is an option for qualifying patients with a higher body mass index (BMI) to help manage or induce remission of the disease.

text_blocks.snippet: You can read more detailed guidelines on Mayo Clinic or review the oral and injectable choices provided by the American Diabetes Association.
